extracted.intended_audience: bank compliance officers, AML/CFT program managers, bank legal/regulatory counsel, and bank supervisors preparing or commenting on the proposed rule
extracted.subtask_description: A section-by-section preamble to a proposed federal rule defining minimum standards and supervisory expectations for banks' Anti‑Money Laundering/Countering the Financing of Terrorism (AML/CFT) programs, including establishment, maintenance, components, and examination/enforcement processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective AML/CFT program (establish and maintain)
rubrics_metrics.description: A bank has an “effective” AML/CFT program if it (1) is established in accordance with the proposed rule's establishment requirements; and (2) is maintained, meaning that a properly established AML/CFT program is implemented in all material respects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The proposed rule frames effectiveness as a two‑pronged requirement (establish + maintain/implement). Minor deficiencies do not necessarily mean failure; only significant or systemic failures to implement an established program would typically warrant an AML/CFT enforcement action or a significant supervisory action. The distinction is intended to focus supervisory/enforcement attention on significant/systemic implementation failures rather than isolated or immaterial issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish versus maintain (design vs implementation)
rubrics_metrics.description: “Establishing” an AML/CFT program involves designing a program that incorporates all required components; “maintaining” addresses whether the bank is implementing that program in practice (the regulation uses the term “implement”).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Separating establishment from maintenance helps distinguish design deficiencies (which require redesign/remediation) from operational deficiencies (which require operational fixes). The distinction affects enforcement thresholds and supervisory criticisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Risk‑based set of internal policies, procedures, and controls (reasonably designed)
rubrics_metrics.description: Banks must establish a risk‑based set of internal policies, procedures, and controls that is reasonably designed to ensure compliance with the BSA and 31 CFR chapter X.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The policies/procedures/controls should be based on and consistent with the bank's risk assessment processes and commensurate with the bank's size, structure, risk profile, and complexity. Reasonably designed gives flexibility in methods and allows adoption of appropriate technology or approaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify, assess, and document ML/TF risks via risk assessment processes
rubrics_metrics.description: As part of the risk‑based internal controls, banks must identify, assess, and document the bank's ML/TF risks through risk assessment processes that evaluate risks of the bank's business activities (products, services, distribution channels, customers, geographic locations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Risk assessment processes must review and, as appropriate, incorporate the AML/CFT Priorities and be updated promptly upon any change the bank knows or has reason to know significantly changes ML/TF risks. Banks may rely on multiple processes and are examined on the totality of processes rather than a single document.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review and appropriate incorporation of AML/CFT Priorities
rubrics_metrics.description: Banks' risk assessment processes must review and, as appropriate, incorporate the AML/CFT Priorities set out by Treasury.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incorporation is required only as appropriate to the bank's risk profile; a perfunctory or surface‑level review will not satisfy the requirement. Banks may focus on specific aspects of a Priority if reasonably justified. Whenever Priorities are updated, banks need only incorporate the most recent Priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prompt updates to risk assessment processes when risk profile changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Banks must update risk assessment processes promptly upon any change that the bank knows or has reason to know would significantly change their ML/TF risk profile.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples prompting updates include new products/services, significant changes to existing offerings, adoption of new risk mitigation technology, geographic expansion/contraction, mergers, acquisitions, divestitures, or relevant external changes. Agencies welcome comment on clarifying timeframes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mitigate ML/TF risks by directing more attention/resources to higher‑risk customers/activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Banks must mitigate ML/TF risks consistent with their risk assessment processes, including by directing more attention and resources toward higher‑risk customers and activities, rather than toward lower‑risk customers and activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This risk‑based allocation is a core element of complying with the AML Act and the proposed rule; agencies will assess whether resource allocation decisions are consistent with reasonably designed risk assessment processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conduct ongoing customer due diligence (CDD)
rubrics_metrics.description: The risk‑based set of internal policies, procedures, and controls must include conducting ongoing customer due diligence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CDD is listed as a primary component of a reasonably designed program; it should be integrated with risk assessment processes and updated as customer risk profiles change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independent AML/CFT program testing
rubrics_metrics.description: Banks must establish independent AML/CFT program testing as part of program establishment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Independent testing is a mechanism both to assess whether the program is implemented effectively and to surface potential implementation deficiencies that would require remediation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designated individual responsible for program (U.S.‑based & accessible)
rubrics_metrics.description: Banks must designate an individual, located in the United States and accessible to FinCEN and the appropriate Agency, responsible for establishing and maintaining the program, and coordinating and monitoring day‑to‑day compliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Simply designating an individual is not sufficient; the bank will be examined for whether that individual is enabling implementation in all material respects, including appropriate allocation of resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ongoing employee training program
rubrics_metrics.description: Banks must establish an ongoing employee training program as part of their AML/CFT program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Training must be maintained and updated consistent with changes to the bank's risk profile and program; a one‑time training program is insufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain program currency as bank's risk profile changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Having an effective AML/CFT program requires keeping the risk‑based internal policies, procedures, controls, and risk assessment processes current as the bank's risk profile changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A previously reasonably designed program may cease to meet establishment requirements if not updated to reflect significant changes (e.g., new customer types or activities identified as high risk). Failure to update may result in supervisory or enforcement action for failure to establish an effective program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flexibility in documentation of risk assessment processes
rubrics_metrics.description: Banks retain flexibility in how they document the results of risk assessment processes; they are not required to establish a single, consolidated risk assessment document.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The term “risk assessment processes” reflects that multiple processes may be relied upon; banks will be examined on the totality of these processes rather than on the sufficiency of a single document.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commensurate design relative to size/complexity/risk profile
rubrics_metrics.description: A bank's risk‑based internal policies, procedures, controls, and risk assessment processes should be commensurate with the size, structure, risk profile, and complexity of the bank.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Large/complex banks are expected to have more formalized/analytically complex processes; smaller or community banks may use more streamlined or qualitative approaches appropriate to their limited risk profile.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure information sources used in risk assessment are reasonably current, complete, and accurate
rubrics_metrics.description: Banks may use internal and external sources (e.g., section 314(b) info‑sharing, FinCEN/regulator feedback, internal device/IP data, Treasury risk assessments) to inform risk assessment processes but should take measures to ensure that such information is reasonably current, complete, and accurate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sources include information from other financial institutions, internal data, and published Treasury/FinCEN analyses like national risk assessments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsible adoption of new technologies / innovation
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies encourage banks to evaluate and responsibly adopt new technology or innovative approaches (e.g., machine learning, GenAI, digital identity, blockchain analytics, APIs) to combat financial crime, but do not require any particular technology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Responsible incorporation of innovative technologies will not by itself increase risk of significant supervisory or enforcement action solely because of the technology's use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency assessment of resource allocation and known resource issues
rubrics_metrics.description: The Agencies will assess whether (1) a bank's resource allocation decisions are consistent with a reasonably designed risk assessment processes; and (2) whether, with respect to implementation, the bank knows or should know of resource‑related issues involving its controls that may result in failure to implement the program and has failed to address such issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies will consider resource adequacy as part of implementation examinations and may treat unaddressed resource constraints that materially affect implementation as supervisory/enforcement concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination focus on implementation in all material respects
rubrics_metrics.description: Banks will be examined for the implementation, in all material aspects, of their established AML/CFT programs, including whether the bank is allocating resources commensurate with its established program and reasonably designed risk assessment processes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Merely having written policies, a designated officer, training and testing programs is insufficient; examiners will evaluate real‑world operation and resource alignment with program design.

rubrics_metrics.name: Common examples of implementation deficiencies
rubrics_metrics.description: Commonly observed examples of ways a bank may fail to implement its AML/CFT program in all material respects include: (1) internal policies/procedures/controls not performed consistently/timely due to inadequate resources; (2) gaps in risk assessment processes that leave high ML/TF risks inadequately covered (e.g., monitoring systems failing to capture material volumes/types of transactions); (3) deficiencies in risk assessment processes that materially impact mitigation due to data issues in relevant processes/systems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These examples are illustrative, not exhaustive, and demonstrate how operational or resource issues can produce material implementation failures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mechanisms to identify implementation concerns
rubrics_metrics.description: Banks could identify implementation‑related concerns through independent testing, examiner observations/suggestions, management information systems and related reports/outputs (e.g., KPIs or KRIs monitoring backlogs), and issues identified by personnel operating the AML/CFT program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These mechanisms should be used proactively to detect, remediate, and document implementation problems before they become systemic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program must be written, accessible, and approved by board or senior management
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed rule discusses requirements that the AML/CFT program be written, accessible, and approved by a bank's Board of Directors, equivalent governing body, or appropriate senior management (see Section IV.E).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Details are addressed in Section IV.E, but the preamble identifies written/accessible/approved program status as an establishment component.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agencies must consult with FinCEN before certain enforcement/supervisory actions
rubrics_metrics.description: The Agencies would be required to give FinCEN written notice at least 30 days prior to taking an AML/CFT enforcement action or a significant AML/CFT supervisory action; FinCEN would have an opportunity to review and provide input regarding the action and underlying information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This procedural change aims to promote consistent approaches to AML/CFT supervision and ensure FinCEN can comment on program effectiveness before significant actions are taken. The enforcement requirements apply only to actions by the Agencies.
